notes: "Human Care Agreement" is the District's standard instrument for direct social/human services, here under OSSE; no runner-up beyond a generic services label.
Mental Health Rehabilitation Services is a clinical benefit delivered to residents; class 918 consulting is the known false lead and the title overrides it.

MBSYEP/TANF youth employment boot camp run by DOES Office of Youth Programs is workforce programming; the only runner-up reading, a coding boot camp, would still be training rather than a technology good or service.

Named vendor product (Ivanti Endpoint Manager) bought through a value-added reseller with no service verb in the title, so licence resale under the reseller rule; runner-up cots_implementation if the award is actually deployment work.
Internship preparation, employer connection and placement for 16-24 year olds is a workforce services program; nothing in title or vendor suggests technology.
Explicit DC Supply Schedule IT equipment and software listing with a $10M ceiling, which authorizes future task orders and buys nothing itself; runner-up hardware_or_license_resale.

"Maintenance & Support" of a named existing system (ESSP) by a benefits-systems software vendor is running software that already exists; runner-up staff_augmentation, rejected because the title names a system and a fixed support scope.
Sidewalk horizontal cutting and restoration is street construction work; no runner-up.

A poverty reduction plan from a policy research firm is social-policy consulting, not advice about technology; runner-up it_consulting_advisory is excluded because the subject matter is not technology.

DDOT sign shop equipment is sign-making plant (printers, plotters, cutters) maintained by a business-equipment dealer, which is shop equipment upkeep rather than IT; runner-up software_om_support or hardware maintenance if the equipment is read as computing gear.

Agilent supplies laboratory analytical instruments and this is an instrument maintenance and service agreement for the medical examiner's lab; the vendor's name plus class 920 is exactly the trap that would push it to software_om_support.
Mental health rehabilitation services delivered to clients by a provider agency; no technology reading available.
Food waste collection is a sanitation service; no runner-up.

"Contract Workspace" is the Ariba term for the contract records in the District's procurement platform, so a $40M OCP award to a solutions vendor reads as deploying and configuring that platform; runner-ups staff_augmentation (procurement support staff) and not_technology (procurement advisory) are both live and the title alone does not settle it.

Bert Smith is a CPA firm and AFM reads as accounting and financial management, so the underlying service is not technology; runner-up ordering_vehicle because it sits on the DC Supply Schedule, which would wrongly count it as technology.
Advertising novelties and promotional products from a printing vendor; no runner-up.
Marketing, media and public information production services; class 961 miscellaneous is uninformative and the title decides it.

A stormwater management and monitoring platform delivered by a systems integrator that builds on commercial platforms; runner-up custom_software_build, which the title cannot rule out since "platform" does not say whether the base product is purchased.
Vocational services for people with disabilities under DDS is a direct human service; no runner-up.
Third-party building plan review for DCRA/DOB is professional engineering review of construction plans; runner-up would be a permitting software reading, which the vendor name does not support.
A named vehicle model (Ford Police Interceptor Utility) bought by DGS is a motor vehicle purchase; no runner-up.
Pavement restoration by a paving contractor for DDOT is road construction; no runner-up.

The goods are promotional novelties, so it is not technology; the runner-up is ordering_vehicle, because 'DCSS' names the DC Supply Schedule and the config's DCSS rule could pull a non-technology schedule contract into that label.

A behavioral health advisor is clinical/programmatic advice, not advice about technology; the runner-up, it_consulting_advisory, is only reachable by trusting class 918 and the word 'Advisor'. Note the contract plainly buys a person's time, but the config forces buys_people to no when work_type is not_technology.

A generic 'Information Technology, Equipment & Software' award by OCP with a $2.85M ceiling matches the DC Supply Schedule pattern the config calls an ordering_vehicle, but the title omits 'DCSS', so hardware_or_license_resale is a live runner-up.
A Human Care Agreement for substance abuse and mental health services is direct service delivery; no runner-up.

A count of 600 units of an electronic device reads as a hardware purchase; the runner-up is cots_implementation, since poll books ship as a vendor product with software that has to be configured for the District.
Residential expenses paid to a care provider for DDS is residential support, not technology; no runner-up.
Electric school buses are vehicles; 'electric' is not information technology, so there is no real runner-up.
Installing modular bus boarding platforms through a construction firm is street construction; no runner-up.

An annual SAS license maintenance renewal bought through a reseller falls under the config's rule that licence and enterprise-agreement renewals are resale; the runner-up is software_om_support, because the word 'Maintenance' points there and the title does not say which of the two it is.
An impartial hearing officer for OSSE's dispute resolution office is a legal/adjudicative service; '_Seat' is the individual vendor's surname, not a seat licence, which is the only trap here.

Inmate phone service from a correctional telecom provider is telecommunications; the $0 value suggests a revenue concession where the District pays nothing, which is why a careful person might argue it is not a technology purchase at all.
'IT Resources' for a named system rebuild (TANF Redesign 2.0 CATCH) is buying labor by the person; the runner-up, custom_software_build, loses because the title buys resources rather than the system.
Laptops and equipment for an agency is a device purchase; no serious runner-up.

'Temporary Personnel Resources' is unambiguously labor, but nothing in the title says the labor is technical: the only technology signal is the word 'Systems' in the vendor name, and the runner-up is not_technology, since DHCF also buys temporary eligibility, call center and clinical staff. This is the exact mirror of the nurse-staffing failure and the fields do not resolve it.
Nuisance abatement for the buildings department is property cleanup and boarding; no runner-up.

Competency-based employee training bought by the human resources agency is workforce training with no technology subject named; a training contract could in principle be IT training, but nothing in the fields says so.

Real estate and financial advisory services from a commercial real estate firm is advice about property and deals, not technology; the runner-up, it_consulting_advisory, is only reachable by reading 'Advisory Services' without its subject.
Deep cleaning and sanitization of a facility is janitorial work; the only trap is the word 'Consulting' in the vendor's name.
